title: Freddie Keppard's trumpet style
summary: Humphrey says the trumpeter was good, between Armstrong and Bunk Johnson in some phrases, with ideas of his own.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles

blocks.x: What did you think of Alfred Freddie as a trumpet player?
He was one of them. What, what, what, do you describe him about his style or anything like that?

Well, it's hard to describe. He'd probably, mostly have to hear the fellow's play. That's right. I'm afraid we won't be able to do that album. He played on a difference between, well, between Lewis Armstrong and, of course, the old-time great. and,
uh, the old-time great. He had, he had,
he had a style of his own, he just went to see. Yeah. Yeah.
Did he sound anything like Buck?
Well, something like Buck. Buck Johnson. Yeah, some, some phrases. Yeah. Yeah, some like Lewis Armstrong. Yeah. And then he had a good many ideas of his own. Yes. Frazes.
